# @vllnt/eslint-config

> ESLint flat config presets for TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, Convex, Turborepo and Playwright, with type-aware rules and Prettier, all at error.

Version 2 needs ESLint >=9 (tested on 9 and 10), Prettier >=3, and the TypeScript 6
JavaScript API (`typescript@npm:@typescript/typescript6@^6.0.2`) for type-aware linting.
Use `@typescript/native@npm:typescript@^7.0.2` alongside it for the TypeScript 7 compiler.
TypeScript 5 is not supported. Every plugin is a dependency of the package. Stable
releases use the npm `latest` tag; `canary` builds are moving prereleases.

## For coding agents

The docs ship inside the package, in `node_modules/@vllnt/eslint-config/`:
`README.md`, `llms.txt` and `CHANGELOG.md`. They match the installed version.
Read them before writing or changing an ESLint config that uses this package.

## When to use

- Use it for a TypeScript project on ESLint 9 or 10 flat config that wants type-aware
  `typescript-eslint` rules, Prettier and import sorting as errors, in React, Next.js,
  Node.js or Convex code, optionally with Turborepo, Playwright or boundaries rules.
- Do not use it when you need warnings or per-preset options (presets take no options;
  every rule is `error`), for `.eslintrc` (ESLint 8 or older), or for type-aware
  linting on TypeScript 5. Compose `typescript-eslint` configs and plugins directly then.

## Entry points

Each entry point exports an array of flat config objects with the same name. Spread it
into `eslint.config.js` and append config objects to change rules. Subpaths also have a
default export; the root entry has named exports only. Full table:
[API reference](./README.md#api).

- `@vllnt/eslint-config`: `base` (and every preset below as a named export)
- `@vllnt/eslint-config/nextjs`: `nextjs`
- `@vllnt/eslint-config/react`: `react`
- `@vllnt/eslint-config/nodejs`: `nodejs`
- `@vllnt/eslint-config/convex`: `convex`
- `@vllnt/eslint-config/turbo`: `turbo` (addition)
- `@vllnt/eslint-config/boundaries`: `boundaries` (addition; needs `settings["boundaries/elements"]`,
  `boundaries/element-types` options and an `import/resolver` that handles `.ts`)
- `@vllnt/eslint-config/playwright`: `playwright` (overlay; spread after a language preset)
- `@vllnt/eslint-config/ignores`: `ignores`

```js
// eslint.config.js
import { nextjs } from "@vllnt/eslint-config/nextjs";

export default [{ ignores: ["eslint.config.js"] }, ...nextjs];
```

The presets turn on `projectService` for every file ESLint lints, `.js` config files
included, so every linted file must be in a `tsconfig.json` or ignored. Without the
`ignores` entry, `eslint .` fails with `Parsing error: .../eslint.config.js was not found
by the project service`.

## Errors and limits

Every message this package defines (the presets' `no-restricted-syntax` messages and the
bundled `convex-rules`), with its cause and fix, and common setup errors:
[Errors and fixes](./README.md#errors-and-fixes). Hard limits and rules that silently do
nothing (`.tsx` naming, `app/api` routes, css-modules, `src/component/` filenames,
`boundaries` rules without options, TypeScript 5.9 from `@convex-dev/eslint-plugin`):
[Limits and gotchas](./README.md#limits-and-gotchas). Peer ranges:
[Compatibility](./README.md#compatibility).

## Diagnostics

From a consuming project, `pnpm exec eslint --inspect-config` opens the Config Inspector,
`TIMING=1 pnpm exec eslint .` prints the slowest rules, and
`pnpm exec eslint . --stats --format json-with-metadata --output-file eslint-stats.json`
records per-file parse and rule timings. See
[Inspecting and profiling ESLint](./README.md#inspecting-and-profiling-eslint).
